inlines.v: Think of it as an upgraded version of ChatGPT. While traditional chatbots can only talk (generate text), OpenClaw can take action. It understands your natural language instructions and can actually perform operations on your computer, such as running commands, managing files, and calling various tools.
Here are some fantastic application scenarios:
Let it help you manage your schedule, set reminders, and track tasks. You just need to tell it in a chat app (like Telegram, WhatsApp), and it will remember and execute.

It can act as a binder for your various services. For example, you can have it monitor a website for price changes. Once a price drop is detected, it can automatically trigger an n8n automation workflow to send you an email notification.
Have it help you manage servers, run scripts, and check logs. You can simply say, "Check the system load for me," and it can SSH into your server, execute the command, and return the results.

This is a very interesting use case. You can have OpenClaw control hardware connected to a Raspberry Pi. For example, a developer used it to control a robotic vacuum cleaner with a mechanical arm, or even had it help analyze racing simulator data and display it on an LED screen. The official Raspberry Pi team even used it to build an automatic photo booth for a wedding, just through conversation, without writing a single line of code!
The Raspberry Pi Zero 2W has only 512MB of RAM, while OpenClaw requires a minimum of 1GB. Therefore, it cannot run properly. A Raspberry Pi 4/5 or higher is recommended.
If you want to experience the power of OpenClaw as quickly as possible, use this method. It will automatically install and launch an interactive setup wizard.
Open the terminal on your Raspberry Pi and run the following command directly. This command downloads the installation script from the official website and executes it:

items.html: curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash

inlines.v: The script will automatically download and install OpenClaw.
You will then see a security prompt asking if you trust OpenClaw. Once you are sure it is safe and reliable, use the arrow keys to navigate to "Yes" and press Enter.
Select Quick Start, and then press Enter.
Select your Model, and then press Enter. Here we use OpenAI as an example.
Fill in the details (Owner, Name, Project, and permissions if needed), then click
Once the key is created, copy it right away — you won't be able to see it again. If you lose it, you'll need to generate a new one.
Paste the key into the OpenClaw configuration.
Select the Model you want to use. In this example, we will use

Next is the channel selection. Channels refer to the communication services supported by OpenClaw, such as Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, and more. Use the down arrow key to select the "Skip for now" option, then press Enter.
Next, you will be prompted to configure skills immediately. Select "Yes" and press Enter.
Install the skills you need. In the following example, we select the "Skip for now" option (press the spacebar to select), then press Enter.
Next are Hooks; we will check "command-logger" and "session-memory".
The installation is now complete. You can start OpenClaw by Selecting "Hatch in TUI" and pressing Enter.
You can start OpenClaw by entering the following command:

blocks.html: openclaw tui

inlines.v: And You can press ctrl+c twice to exit the tui interface.

PiCar-X Skill is an extension for OpenClaw that allows you to control your SunFounder PiCar-X robot car through natural language. Instead of writing Python scripts or remembering servo angles, you can simply tell OpenClaw what you want PiCar-X to do — like "drive forward", "check what's ahead", or "turn left" — and OpenClaw will execute the appropriate Python code automatically.
Here are some things you can do with PiCar-X Skill:
Drive forward, backward, turn left/right with steering servo control
Pan left/right, tilt up/down via the 2-axis camera gimbal
Read ultrasonic distance, grayscale sensor data for line tracking and cliff detection
Play sound effects and music through the car's speaker
Take photos, detect faces, track colors, recognize QR codes, gestures, and traffic signs
Before you can use PiCar-X Skill with OpenClaw, make sure you have:
properly assembled and connected to your Raspberry Pi
You can verify the installation by running:

blocks.html: python3 -c "import picarx"

inlines.v: If this command runs without errors, you're ready to proceed.
Follow these steps to install the PiCar-X Skill for OpenClaw:

items.html: cp -r ~/picar-x/picarx-control ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/
ls ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/picarx-control/

inlines.v: file contains all the instructions OpenClaw needs — safety rules, code templates for each capability, and a mapping from natural language requests to Python code. OpenClaw reads this file and uses it to decide what code to execute on your PiCar-X.

inlines.v: Before using the skill with OpenClaw, you may want to test basic functionality directly from the terminal using the included CLI tool.

python3 ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/picarx-control/scripts/pc.py move forward --speed 60

Q. During installation, I get the error
Error: systemctl is-enabled unavailable: Command failed: systemctl --user is-enabled openclaw-gateway.service
You can ignore this for now, but you might encounter issues in the next steps. Please refer to them one by one at that time.

blocks.html:
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc

inlines.v: You should now be able to start the tui interface with
not connected to gateway — message not sent
This is because your OpenClaw Gateway service is not started. Open another terminal and execute the following command to start the OpenClaw Gateway:

blocks.html: openclaw gateway

inlines.v: , and you can use it directly.
Q. I want to set the OpenClaw Gateway service to run in the background / start automatically on boot. How do I do that?
Normally, your OpenClaw Gateway service should start automatically on boot. If it doesn't, you can manually start it with the following command.

blocks.html: mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user

blocks.code:
cat > ~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service << EOF
[Unit]
Description=OpenClaw Gateway
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=$HOME/.npm-global/bin/openclaw gateway run
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=10
Environment="PATH=$HOME/.npm-global/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin"
Environment="NODE_ENV=production"

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
EOF
blocks.html:
cat > ~/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service << EOF
[Unit]

After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=$HOME/.npm-global/bin/openclaw gateway run
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=10
Environment="PATH=$HOME/.npm-global/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin"
Environment="NODE_ENV=production"

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
EOF
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user start openclaw-gateway

inlines.v: , and you can use it directly.
Enable it to start on boot:

blocks.html: systemctl --user enable openclaw-gateway

inlines.v: Q. My OpenClaw can not operate the system, what should I do?
A newly installed OpenClaw may not have permission to operate your Raspberry Pi system by default; it can only chat. We need to manually configure the permissions.

blocks.html: nano ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json

"tools": {
    "profile": "coding",
    "exec": {
        "secrity": "full"
    }
},

inlines.v: Enter the following command in the terminal to restart the OpenClaw Gateway:

blocks.html: openclaw gateway restart

inlines.v: Now, OpenClaw should have read and write permissions and be able to operate your Raspberry Pi system.
Q. PiCar-X doesn't respond to commands. What should I do?
First, verify that PiCar-X is properly connected and powered on. Then test basic functionality:

blocks.html: python3 ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/picarx-control/scripts/pc.py sensor distance

inlines.v: If this fails, ensure the required Python libraries are installed:

blocks.code: python3 -c "import picarx; import robot_hat; import vilib"
blocks.html: python3 -c "import picarx; import robot_hat; import vilib"

inlines.v: This means the PiCar-X Python library is not properly installed. Please refer to the PiCar-X official installation guide to install the necessary libraries. You can also run the included install script:

blocks.html: bash ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/picarx-control/install.sh

inlines.v: Q. OpenClaw doesn't recognize the PiCar-X skill.
Remind OpenClaw to sync the skills by saying in the TUI:

blocks.html: openclaw gateway restart

inlines.v: Q. PiCar-X movements seem jerky or the steering is off-center.
This is usually caused by servo calibration values being incorrect. Run the calibration script to adjust the steering servo and camera gimbal:

blocks.html: python3 ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/picarx-control/scripts/pc.py calibrate

inlines.v: You can also adjust the speed parameter (e.g., use
) for smoother movement, or add short delays between consecutive commands.
Q. The grayscale or line tracking doesn't work properly.

Make sure the grayscale module is properly calibrated for your surface. You can set the line reference values using the configuration. Refer to the main PiCar-X documentation for grayscale calibration procedures.
